data.q: What is the primary difference between a C# record and a class regarding equality?
o: Records use reference equality; classes use value equality
Records use value-based equality; classes use reference equality by default
data.e: Records implement value-based equality (comparing all properties), while classes use reference equality by default unless overridden.

data.q: Which syntax declares a positional record with two properties?
o: record Person { string Name; int Age; }
record Person { get; set; string Name; get; set; int Age; }
data.e: Positional records use the constructor-like syntax: `record TypeName(Param1, Param2);` which automatically creates init-only properties and a primary constructor.

data.q: What does the 'with' expression do on a record?
o: Creates a new record instance with specified properties modified
Deconstructs a record into its components
data.e: The `with` expression creates a new record instance (non-destructive mutation) copying all properties from the original and applying specified changes.

data.q: Can a record inherit from another record?
o: Yes, records support inheritance from other records
Only if the base record is marked 'abstract'
data.e: Records can inherit from other records (but not from classes). The derived record must include base constructor parameters.

data.q: What is the default behavior of a record struct regarding equality?
data.e: Record structs (and records) implement value-based equality by comparing all fields/properties automatically.

data.q: Which of the following is true about record immutability?
o: Records are fully immutable by default
Positional records have init-only properties by default, but nominal records can have mutable properties
data.e: Positional records generate init-only properties. Nominal records (with braces) allow mutable properties unless explicitly made init-only.

data.q: How does a record's ToString() method differ from a class's default ToString()?
o: Records print the type name only
Records print a formatted string with property names and values
data.e: Records override ToString() to output a formatted representation like `Person { Name = "John", Age = 30 }`.

data.q: What is the correct way to deconstruct a record?
data.e: Records automatically generate a Deconstruct method, allowing both positional deconstruction syntax and explicit Deconstruct calls.

data.q: Which modifier prevents a record from being inherited?
data.e: The `sealed` modifier prevents inheritance of records, just like with classes.

data.q: What happens when you compare two record instances with == operator?
o: Compares all properties for value equality
data.e: Records override == and != operators to perform value-based equality comparison of all properties.

data.q: Can a record implement an interface?
o: Only record structs can implement interfaces
Only if the record is sealed
data.e: Records can implement interfaces just like classes.

data.q: What is the difference between 'record' and 'record struct'?
o: record is a reference type; record struct is a value type
They are identical, just different syntax
data.e: `record` declares a reference type (class-like), while `record struct` declares a value type (struct-like) with record semantics.

data.q: How are init-only properties different from readonly properties?
o: init-only can be set during object initialization; readonly only in constructor
data.e: init-only properties can be set via object initializers and with-expressions; readonly fields can only be assigned in constructors.

data.q: What does the 'required' keyword on a record property enforce?
o: The property must be initialized at creation (constructor or initializer)
The property must have a default value
data.e: Required properties (C# 11+) must be initialized either in the constructor or via object initializer, otherwise a compile-time warning/error occurs.

data.q: Which statement about record equality is FALSE?
o: Two records of different types are never equal
Record equality is recursive for nested records
data.e: Record equality considers property order (matching positional parameters). Two records with same values but different property declaration order are not equal.

data.q: What is the performance characteristic of record struct vs record (class)?
o: record struct avoids heap allocation; record allocates on heap
record struct causes more GC pressure
data.e: record struct is a value type allocated on the stack (or inline in arrays), avoiding heap allocation and GC pressure. record is a reference type allocated on the heap.
